newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal - Light pre-holiday sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal - Light pre-holiday sales.

text.p: Some soymeal rail basis offers were lower again Wednesday, but dealers reported a slight increase in sales as livestock interests bought supplies to cover needs during the Memorial Day holiday week.

A few dealers said the slight increase in sales was also partially motivated by a decline in cash prices since last week. Soymeal delivered to some customers was now near $300 per ton, which appealed to buyers.
"This is the first time in a long time we are seeing the delivered price at $300 (per ton) instead of $320," said a Midwest dealer.
CBOT July soymeal futures closed Tuesday at $285.30 per ton, the lowest close since May 1. At 1115 CDT, July soybean was down $1.00 at $284.30.
Hog and turkey producers continue to be steady buyers of soymeal, but dairy farms appeared to be substituting lower-priced feed ingredients for soymeal.
